evidence: tools/check_steps.py:478-486: `if code == 0: ... inputs, why = inputs_of(trace, self.memo)` then `save_json(self.entry_path(step["key"]), {... "inputs": inputs, "output": output ...})`. inputs_of (:317-334) computes `memo.digest(p)` at that moment, after the process exited. hazards() (:496-529), which runs after all steps (:575), only prints a WARNING and learns the writer (`found.append(conflict); self.learned.add(command)`). It never invalidates the cache entry of the step that read the file mid-write, and never fails the run.
fix: Have the tracer record each file's content digest when it is opened (or record (size, mtime_ns) at open and compare it at key time), and refuse to cache a step when any input's state at the end differs from its state at open. Also delete the cache entries of every step that hazards() names (reader and writer) for the run in which a hazard was found.

reviewer: tools/check_steps.py:478-486 computes inputs_of only after process.wait(). FileMemo.digest (:275-293) restats size/mtime and rehashes, so it records the file's post-run content. hazards() (:496-529) runs after all steps. It only adds the writer to self.learned and prints a WARNING (:577-579), and never unlinks the reader's cache entry. On the next run, inputs_unchanged replays the reader's PASS against bytes it never judged. This holds when a parallel step that is not yet a known writer, or an outside edit, changes a read file during the run. The writer is serialized from the next run on, but the poisoned reader entry survives until the input changes again.
scenario: Step A (a reader such as current_view --check) reads planning/proofs.json at version v1 and passes. During the same parallel `make check`, step B (a writer not yet in WRITERS or writers.json), or a person or lane editing the worktree, rewrites proofs.json to v2 before A's key is computed. A's cache entry records digest(v2) with A's PASS. On the next `make check` proofs.json is still v2, so inputs_unchanged() is true and A is replayed as "cached (inputs unchanged since <sha>)" exit 0. A has never judged v2. The hazard run itself only prints a warning, so the stale verdict persists until v2 changes again. The only protection is a FORCE=1 run.
title: check_steps caches a PASS under input digests taken after the step finished, including runs that hit a write hazard
